business_summary: Alphabet is classed as an internet platforms company. The evidence supplied is financial only: a FY25 operating margin of 37.28%, ROCE of 34.4% and debt/equity of 0.12x. No segment detail or investor documents were provided, so this summary does not describe products or revenue mix.
why_own: The evidence shows a highly profitable, low-debt business (ROE 35.7%, operating margin 37.28%) that has grown revenue 12.51% a year over 3 years with profits growing faster (30.14% a year). The case rests on numbers alone because no investor documents were supplied, so it has no qualitative drivers, and it is untested against the stock's own valuation history.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently 12.51%, versus 17.15% over 5 years).
Operating margin stays high (37.28% in FY25, up 6.05 pp over 3 years), so growth keeps converting into profit.
Returns on capital stay well above typical levels (ROCE 34.4%, ROE 35.7%) with little leverage (debt/equity 0.12x).
Reported profit is backed by cash: operating cash flow was 1.25 times net profit in FY25.

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 25%, well under the FY25 level of 37.28%.
ROCE falls below 15%, less than half the FY25 level of 34.4%.

risks.statement: Price/book is 10.02x, so the valuation depends on returns staying near current levels (ROE 35.7%). The P/E comparison with the stock's own history is not available (n/a), so whether the current 17.04x trailing P/E is high or low relative to history is untested.
Revenue growth over 3 years (12.51% a year) is below the 5-year rate (17.15% a year), so growth may be slowing. The evidence does not say why.

Trailing-4-quarter net profit (244,205 USD m) is far above FY25 net profit (132,170 USD m). The evidence does not explain the gap, so the trailing P/E of 17.04x rests on a profit base that has not been tested. No quarter in the last 4 was loss-making.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if FY25 is a cyclical high in margins and growth, not a base. Revenue growth has already slowed from 17.15% (5y) to 12.51% (3y). Profit grew 30.14% a year against revenue's 12.51%, so margin expansion drove it, and that cannot repeat. The thresholds are lenient: operating margin must fall from 37.28% to below 27% before D2 breaks, and revenue growth to 7%, with nothing flagged along the way. Valuation (P/B 10.02x) assumes returns stay near 35%. The 17.04x trailing P/E rests on trailing profit that is 1.85x the fiscal-year figure, unexplained. Evidence is financial only, so there is no check on why any of this holds. What would change this view: Evidence that the trailing profit of 244,205 USD m is recurring operating earnings, and that revenue growth and operating margin have held at or above FY25 levels in the latest quarters, would remove most of this objection.
